version.changelog: v7.1: 自记忆引擎 — 系统记住自己的每一次迭代

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: long-memory
Version: 7.1.0

The bundle provides a highly complex memory management system with several high-risk capabilities that, while aligned with its stated purpose, create a significant attack surface. Key indicators include 'auto_backup.py', which uses subprocesses to execute Git commands (including pushing data to remote repositories), and 'api_server.py', which starts a local HTTP server to expose conversation logs via a REST API. Additionally, 'privacy.py' claims to implement AES-256 encryption in its documentation but actually uses a weak, non-standard XOR-based cipher, which is a significant security discrepancy. The 'capture_session.py' script also performs broad file reads from the user's home directory (~/.openclaw/sessions) to archive data.

llm.summary: The package largely matches its 'long memory' description, but it reads local OpenClaw session files, writes persistent archives to your home directory, exposes a local HTTP API, and can auto-push archives to a Git remote — behaviour that is coherent with backup/archival features but carries privacy/exfiltration risk and a few minor mismatches with the textual claims.

dimensions.detail: The name/description align with the provided scripts: CLI tooling, session capture, archiving, multiple search engines, a local REST API, encryption and auto-backup. One minor mismatch: the README/description claim saving the assistant's '思考过程' (internal thought process); the capture code records assistant messages and skips system messages, so it will archive assistant outputs present in session files but will not magically capture private internal chain-of-thought that the model never emitted. Otherwise capabilities are coherent with a conversation memory tool.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime code will read OpenClaw session files (~/.openclaw/sessions), write archives to a memory directory (default ~/.openclaw/workspace/memory), and can launch a local HTTP API bound to 127.0.0.1:8765. The auto-backup feature will run git commit/push from the memory directory and can push to a configured remote, which could transfer all stored conversations off-host if the user configures a remote (or has credentials available). These operations are within the stated purpose but have significant privacy/egress implications and should be enabled only with caution.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No installation spec — instruction-only plus included Python scripts. That is lower risk than arbitrary remote installers. The package contains many scripts that will be written to disk when the skill is installed or unpacked, but there is no automatic remote download/execute step in the provided metadata.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials, which is consistent. However, several behaviors implicitly use local credentials/configuration: git push will rely on the user's configured Git credentials (SSH keys, credential helper, or remote with embedded credentials), and the REST API and file I/O operate on files under the user's home directory. This is proportional to a backup/archive tool but raises the usual concerns about where sensitive memories are stored and where they might be pushed.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill persists data to the user's filesystem and can initialize a git repo and set git user config in the memory directory. It does not declare 'always: true' and does not appear to modify other skills or system-wide agent settings, but it does create/modify files in ~/.openclaw/workspace/memory (by default) and may create archives, backups, and audit logs — all expected for its purpose but persistent and potentially large.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to implement what it promises, but exercise caution before enabling it: 1) Review and set long-memory.json and start the tool with a memory_dir you control (do not use a directory with other sensitive files). 2) Keep auto_backup disabled until you understand where it would push; a configured Git remote or credentials could cause all archived conversations to be exfiltrated. 3) If you need encryption, inspect scripts/privacy.py to confirm AES-256 is implemented correctly and enable it for any sensitive entries. 4) The skill reads ~/.openclaw/sessions to capture conversations — if you don't want that, don't run capture_session or change the sessions path. 5) The REST API listens on 127.0.0.1:8765 by default; only bind it to localhost and do not expose it publicly. 6) The repository contains many omitted files in this review; if you plan to install, run the test suite locally (python3 -m pytest tests/) and manually inspect privacy/auto_backup/api_server code for any network calls or credential usage before enabling backups or API. If you are unsure about secrets or compliance, treat this skill as capable of persisting and (with configuration) transmitting your conversation data and proceed only after applying the safeguards above.
